symphony.gloss: An extended piece of music of sophisticated structure, usually for orchestra.

symptom.gloss: (medicine) A perceived change in some function, sensation or appearance of a person that indicates a disease or disorder, such as fever, headache or rash; strictly, a symptom is felt or experienced by the patient, while a sign can be detect

synagogue.gloss: (countable, Judaism) A place of worship for Jews or Samaritans.
(countable, Judaism) A congregation of Jews or Samaritans for the purpose of worship or religious study.

synapse.gloss: The junction between the terminal of a neuron and either another neuron or a muscle or gland cell, over which nerve impulses pass.

synchronised swimming.gloss: A swimming event where competitors swim in a ballet-like manner in a swimming pool

synchronization.gloss: The state or property of being synchronized.

synchronized swimming.gloss: A swimming event where swimmers perform a synchronised routine of dance moves in the water.

syncopation.gloss: (music) The quality of a rhythm being somehow unexpected, in that it deviates from the strict succession of regularly spaced strong and weak beats in a meter.

syncope.gloss: (linguistics, phonology, prosody) The elision or loss of a sound from the interior of a word, especially of a vowel sound with loss of a syllable.
(music) A missed beat or off-beat stress in music resulting in syncopation.

syncytiotrophoblast.gloss: (cytology) The outer layer of the trophoblast, consisting of a single cell with many nuclei and a very large size and surface area.

syndicate.gloss: (crime) A group of gangsters engaged in organized crime.

syndrome.gloss: (pathology) A recognizable pattern of signs, symptoms and/or behaviours, especially of a disease or medical or psychological condition.
Any set of characteristics regarded as identifying a certain type, condition, etc., usually adverse.

synecdoche.gloss: (figure of speech) A figure of speech that uses the name of a part of something to represent the whole, or the whole to represent a part, or a specific kind or instance to represent the general category, or the general category to represent

synod.gloss: (Christianity) An ecclesiastic council or meeting to consult on church matters.

synonym.gloss: (taxonomy, by extension) Any name that has been applied to a taxon other than the one to be used, including those not allowed by the rules such as misspellings or nomina nuda.

synonymous.gloss: (particularly, in, semantics, construed with with) Having a similar (sometimes identical) meaning. (See Usage notes below)

synopsis.gloss: (authorship) A brief summary of the major points of a written work, either as prose or as a table; an abridgment or condensation of a work.

syntagma.gloss: (linguistics) A constituent segment within a text, such as a word or a phrase that forms a syntactic unit.

syntax.gloss: A set of rules that govern how words are combined to form phrases and sentences.

synthesis.gloss: The formation of something complex or coherent by combining simpler things.

synthesizer.gloss: (musical instrument) An electronic musical instrument that creates its sounds with electronics and generally is played via a keyboard.

syphilis.gloss: (disease) A disease spread via sexual activity, caused by the bacterium Treponema pallidum.

syracuse.gloss: A city and port, the capital of the province of Syracuse, Sicily, Italy.

syria.gloss: A country in West Asia in the Middle East. Official name: Syrian Arab Republic. Capital: Damascus.

syringe.gloss: A device consisting of a hypodermic needle, a chamber for containing liquids, and a piston for applying pressure (to inject) or reducing pressure (to draw); a hypodermic syringe.

syrup.gloss: Any thick liquid that has a high sugar content and which is added to or poured over food as a flavoring.

system.gloss: A group or set of related things that operate together as a complex whole. [from early 17th c.]

systematics.gloss: The classification system of a branch of science, especially the classification of organisms in biology.

syvash.gloss: (as Syvash) A former village in Pervomaiskyi miskrada, Kharkiv Oblast, Ukraine, first mentioned in 1777, annexed to the city of Pervomaiskyi (now Zlatopil) in July 1994.

syvaske.gloss: A rural settlement in Novotroitske settlement hromada, Henichesk Raion, Kherson Oblast, Ukraine, founded in 1816.

szczecin.gloss: A city in what is now Poland; the capital of West Pomeranian Voivodeship; Stettin.

são paulo.gloss: A municipality, the state capital of São Paulo State, Brazil.

são tomé and príncipe.gloss: A country and archipelago of Central Africa in the Atlantic Ocean. Official name: Democratic Republic of São Tomé and Príncipe. Capital: São Tomé.

séance.gloss: A ceremony where people try to communicate with the spirits of dead people, usually led by a medium.

sōma.gloss: A city in Fukushima Prefecture, Japan.
